{"description":"Interactive worktree sessions - run multiple Claude Code instances on different tasks in parallel.

## Use Case
User opens 2+ terminals, each working on a separate task in its own worktree.
Each terminal has full LETS workflow: /lets:start, /lets:commit, /lets:done.

## Key Problem
Agent worktrees (isolation:worktree) don't need .lets/ - agents only do code work.
Interactive worktrees DO need .lets/ - user runs LETS commands.
But worktrees are in .lets/worktrees/ - symlink creates circular path.

## Options to Resolve
A) Interactive worktrees in different location (.worktrees/ at project root) + .lets/ symlink
B) Detect interactive vs agent in WorktreeCreate hook (different stdin context?)
C) Use claude --worktree flag (creates in .claude/worktrees/) + separate hook behavior
D) Shared .lets/ via MAIN_ROOT detection in commands (no symlink)

## Implementation
- New command: commands/worktree.md
- Subcommands: create, list, remove, info
- Uses bd worktree create for beads redirect
- Handles .lets/ access for interactive sessions
- Verify .gitignore before creating
- Show LETS box with next steps

## Test Scenario
1. Terminal 1: normal session on task A
2. Terminal 2: claude --worktree (or /lets:worktree create)
3. Terminal 2: /lets:start -> pick task B -> work -> /lets:commit
4. Verify: shared beads, shared .lets/config.yaml, independent sessions
